q: Along with Perrières and Genevrières, which climat completes Meursault's most-cited trio of premiers crus?
exp: Perrières is the perennial grand-cru candidate.

q: What is the Paulée de Meursault?
ans: The great harvest-end banquet of Meursault (third of the Trois Glorieuses)
exp: Hospices de Beaune auction Sunday, Clos de Vougeot dinner Saturday, La Paulée Monday.

q: The Hospices de Beaune charity auction is held on the third Sunday of which month?
exp: Since 1859; barrels sell under the buyer's name with the Hospices cuvée label.

q: Match the grand cru to its commune.
ans: Clos de la Roche–Morey · Grands Échezeaux–Flagey · Ruchottes–Gevrey · La Grande Rue–Vosne
exp: La Grande Rue (Lamarche monopole) runs between La Tâche and Romanée-Conti.

q: Which Beaujolais cru is generally reckoned the most structured and age-worthy?
exp: Manganese-rich granite; old bottles pass for Côte de Beaune Pinot.

q: Aligoté finally received its own cru-level recognition through which village AOP?
exp: A. et P. de Villaine made its case; classic base of Kir with crème de cassis.

q: What percentage of Chardonnay may a red Corton legally contain?
exp: Corton rouge may include up to 15% Chardonnay — rarely used but legal.

q: Name the two Burgundy domaines run by Lalou Bize-Leroy.
exp: She co-directed DRC until 1992; Domaine Leroy is biodynamic and stratospheric.

q: A bottle costs $19 wholesale; the program targets 28% cost. List price?
exp: Cost ÷ target% = price; round to the list's ladder.

q: A 5-oz glass sells at $16 from a $48-wholesale 750 ml bottle. What is the pour cost %?
ans: $48/5 pours = $9.60 cost per glass → 9.60/16 = 60% — a money-loser
exp: Always sanity-check BTG math per pour, not per bottle.

q: Define 'variance' in beverage inventory and its top three causes.
accept: difference between actual and theoretical usage overpour spillage theft
ans: Actual usage vs POS-theoretical usage; causes: overpouring, spillage/waste, theft (plus ringing errors)
exp: Run it monthly by category; 1–2% is livable, 5% is a hole.

q: Calculate: a 6-course tasting menu pairs 3-oz pours. How many covers does one bottle serve per course?
exp: Pairing math drives par orders: 40 covers = 5 bottles per course.

q: The three-tier system's tiers, and the notable control-state twist:
accept: supplier distributor retailer control states government wholesale
producer wholesaler retailer some states run the middle
ans: Producer/importer → distributor → retailer; in control states, government runs wholesale (and sometimes retail)
exp: Post-Prohibition architecture; direct-to-consumer carves grow yearly.
